the evil dragons shall withdraw their venom and no longer harm people.
Wearing and binding this vow-thread brings such immediate retribution as described above. The name of the first deity is Panapadi; his title is "The Spirit of Refinement, Vigor, and Courage.

The name of the second deity is Sarapadi; his title is "The Savior of the World. The name of the third deity is Sāvakara; his title is "The One Free from Deviant Conduct. The name of the fourth deity is Nicilouli; his title is "The One Who Extinguishes Discursive Thought. The name of the fifth deity is Paropanran; his title is "The Majestic and Resplendent One. The name of the sixth deity is Hilan-tanqi; his title is "The One Like the Ocean and Rivers. The name of the seventh deity is Jinlai-yitou; his title is "The One Fearless of Armies. These seven spirit-kings shall employ their majestic spiritual powers.
The Lord pursued those who falsely claimed to be wandering spirits whose names were not yet registered in the records—
beings neither governed by the heavens nor admitted into hell, yet coming and going within the world—
whether they were in cities, towns, villages, or hamlets.
They manifest various strange and monstrous transformations to terrify and unsettle people's hearts.
Foolish people, filled with panic and fear, prepare offerings of merit for them, calling them "gods.
Some say, "Your life belongs to me; I shall inflict various ailments upon you to ensure you do not die."
By means of the name of the deity who binds and wears the cord,
these evil spirits will no longer harass or approach to demand food or drink from people.
Because of the power of the merit resulting from wearing and binding the cord with such vows, the retribution is manifested in this very life.

The deity named Jirana-raiya, whose style name is Tongda-xianshen; the deity named Juanmo-zhilou, whose style name is Jianzheng-chuang; the deity named Niehe-wu-he, whose style name is Zhida-qi; the deity named Ju-tou-mahei, whose style name is Zuishang-sheng; the deity named Chatali-che, whose style name is Jiuxingjian; the deity named Nantou-yunan, whose style name is Jixian-ning; and the deity named Xichi-xichi, whose style name is Shili-qiang—these seven spirit-kings shall employ their majestic spiritual power.
It primarily treats flying poisons (*fei-shi*), the ghosts of external qi (*ke-qi*), and recurring or continuous demonic afflictions (*fu-lian-zhu-gui*).
It is also for those cases where seductive demons (*mei-gui*) enter a person’s body and cause the mind to become disturbed,
such that decoctions, medicinal herbs, acupuncture, and moxibustion are all ineffective, and incantations fail to take effect.
This ghost circulates within the hundred joints and five channels of human beings,
causing people to be bewildered and preventing various treatments from being effective.
By wearing this amulet and upholding the name of the deity with a firm vow, [one shall be protected].
These various ghost-demons will be unable to cause harm. Such is the manifest retribution for the merit of one’s vows.

The name of the deity is Aparijita, whose title is Infinite Wisdom; the name of the deity is Kautiśeya, whose title is Severer of All Bonds; the name of the deity is Mārimara, whose title is Abiding Righteous Minister; the name of the deity is Aniruddha, whose title is Accumulator of Wealth and Bestower; the name of the deity is Paniruddha, whose title is Non-Abandoner of Vows; the name of the deity is Aghora-mati, whose title is Remover of Defilements; the name of the deity is Adumari, whose title is Sincere and Faithful. These seven divine kings shall, by means of their majestic spiritual power, [protect you].
The Master entered among the streams, valleys, mountains, and wilds.
There were venomous snakes, vipers, and various other poisonous insects;
as well as elephants, dragons, bears, brown bears, tigers, wolves, and other beasts.
May those who devour human flesh and blood out of various fears and terrors,
by means of the name of this protective deity bound by vows and worn as an amulet,
constantly follow [the practitioner] at their side to act as a guardian for them.
By eliminating all evils, one shall be free from manifold decline and affliction. Wearing [this] and maintaining the vow brings such present retribution.

The deity named Akajiti, whose epithet is *Zhengzhenzhi* (Correct and True Healing); The deity named Subhāri, whose epithet is *Zhengzhushen* (Correctly Abiding Peace); The deity named Carabira, whose epithet is *Fumochimei* (Subduing Demons and Spirits); The deity named Ahabila, whose epithet is *Jiaolingcong* (Following the Teachings and Commands); The deity named Baramaju, whose epithet is *Langhezhao* (Brilliant and Radiant Illumination); The deity named Śrāmadhi, whose epithet is *Yanjingzhu* (Dignified and Orderly Abiding); The deity named Tajinili, whose epithet is *Lianaming* (Established in Peaceful Brilliance). These seven spirit-kings shall, by means of their majestic spiritual power, [protect you].
It primarily treats those who invade and oppress the borders as rebels,
who plunder the wealth and treasures of others with intent to steal,
and who constantly harbor evil thoughts without ceasing.
Due to greedy seeking, they ruin the king’s realm;
villages, camps, and market towns further harass and harm one another.
By means of wearing this amulet and invoking the name of the deity who binds vows, [one attains protection].
Enemies, bandits, and their associates from the ten directions will naturally vanish and be unable to cause harm;
such is the manifest retribution for wearing, carrying, and making vows with this sūtra.

The deity named Nidhāpanī, whose epithet is Viśeṣa; the deity named Nirbhatsanī, whose epithet is Gambhīra-nirvāṇa; the deity named Mahāmanas, whose epithet is Padavyañjana; the deity named Anuttarīṇa, whose epithet is Vijñapti-taraṇa; the deity named Oṇatindu, whose epithet is Kṣema-sthira; the deity named Oṇatida, whose epithet is Gaganastha; and the deity named Omititu, whose epithet is Dhāraṇī-vidyā-mantra—these seven divine kings shall act through their majestic spiritual power.
Within the protected realm,
there are various poisonous vapors that strike the human body; upon being struck,
one immediately experiences chills and fever, and various swellings arise, sometimes even penetrating to the bone.
By the time it bursts open, the thick blood and putrid stench are such that one cannot approach it.
Even if one recites incantations over saliva, they will have no effect, and sometimes death ensues.
Such toxic harm arises in the midst of the final age.
Because this person wears and maintains this Sūtra of Boundless Vows,
the poisons of impure vapors shall not harm their body; they shall ward off and eliminate all evils,
and no malevolent demons or heterodox spirits shall dare to confront them.
Thus is the immediate retribution for wearing, carrying, and making vows.
The Buddha told Śakra, Lord of the Devas: "If there are men or women who have been seized by malevolent spirits or ghosts..."
One should wash one's hands and rinse one's mouth to become pure;
with a focused mind, pay reverent homage to the Buddhas and the Triple Gem,
and burn various famous incenses, such as resin incense, *bō* incense, and *anxi* incense.
The ground is smeared with fragrant liquid to a length and breadth of seven feet;
five-colored flowers are scattered, and lamps are lit in the ten directions.
Seven strands each of five-colored thread are used.
Take a seven-foot-long cord and bind it on the left side.
Also, write out the names of the hundred deities who protect the kingdom and tie them together as well.
If there is anyone who receives this, they should kneel long and join their palms.
Focus your mind single-mindedly on the Triple Gem and do not think of matters concerning the directions of east, west, south, or north.
Furthermore, do not think of matters concerning your family or household.
Listen to what the Master says and receive it with bowed head and deep reverence, O Kings of the Ghost Spirits.
One should, by means of one's own majestic power, provide great protection and assistance to men and women.
If it is worn upon the body while walking, coming, going, or entering,
then all classes of ghosts and demons who hear or see it [shall be subdued].
They fled in all directions, each hiding themselves and keeping their distance from people.
The Buddha told Śakra, Lord of the Devas: "These hundred kṣetrapāla kings of the consecrated verses are not merely summoned by tying threads and calling out their names."
If a person is afflicted by perilous calamities or various hardships,
they should call upon and keep in mind whichever deity they primarily worship;
that deity will always remain at their side, never departing for even a moment.
By writing and maintaining these names, one may suppress and eliminate inauspiciousness.
Following the divine protection, a hundred monsters shall be extinguished;
no demonic or heterodox forces dare to oppose it, and there shall be nothing but auspiciousness.
They shall transcend all calamities and their lifespans will be extended.
When the Buddha spoke the names of the hundred kings of the *śatasāhasrikā* chapter on consecration (*abhiṣeka*),
eight bodhisattvas came from other directions.
He prostrated at the Buddha's feet and asked the Buddha, saying:
"The names of these deities are such that few other king-deities can equal them.
O God among Gods, Tathāgata, it is you who have spoken these names of the deities."
Those bodhisattvas who delight in diligence practice without indolence.
After the Buddha’s parinirvāṇa, will these divine kings remain for a long time within Jambudvīpa?
The Buddha told the eight bodhisattvas:
"After my parinirvāṇa, these various kings of spirits shall appear in the world for two hundred years, reaching up to three hundred years; thereafter, they will no longer appear."
In the future, during an age of turbidity and chaos when the Buddha’s scriptures are about to perish,
the assembly of bhikṣus will no longer employ the Dharma, proper decorum, or the precepts;
they will constantly harbor mutual jealousy and destroy the true transformation.
When my Dharma has perished and the various kingdoms are at war with one another,
the deity named Jielü (Knot-Thread) shall manifest once more.
Toward the end of the Buddha-dharma, there will be some bhikṣus who have studied only a little.
It is by the Buddha’s majestic spiritual power that this sutra is recited.
The elder bhikṣus do not wish to hear it,
addressing those bhikṣus who have studied for only a short time.
"You have destroyed the Buddha-dharma by practicing this false view;
you shall fall into the realm of ghosts and spirits as well as the hells.
You should know that the Buddha-dharma will gradually perish from here."
At that time, there were the Bodhisattvas Mahāsusārtha, Kautūhala, Naradatta, and Susīma.
The Bodhisattva Huilin and others addressed the Buddha together, saying:
"O God among Gods, in the time after the *parinirvāṇa*, when the world has passed away..."
We shall protect and uphold this sutra scroll so that the Buddha-way may endure for a long time.
If there are those who have not yet heard this scripture,
we shall initiate them, instructing them to recite, proclaim, and maintain it.
The Buddha addressed Ānanda, Śakra Devendra, and the fourfold assembly of disciples:
"This Bhadrapāla, a teacher among five hundred bodhisattvas, shall uphold the True Dharma."
All who gathered followed and complied with the teaching without exception;
with joyful hearts, compliant minds, and pure hearts, they cast away their desires.
At that time, five hundred people all stood before the Buddha with their palms joined.
The Bodhisattva Bhadrapāla addressed the Buddha, saying,
"By how many matters does a bodhisattva maintain [the practice] so as to be able to perform this divine mantra?
The Buddha said, "There are four matters by which one can perform this divine mantra."
First, not believing in other paths;
second, severing craving and desire;
third, practicing in accordance with the Dharma.
Fourth is the absence of covetousness in birth.
If a bodhisattva practices these four matters,
they will then be able to obtain this *Abhiṣeka-mantra-saṃkalpa-mahāvidyā-sūtra*.
The Buddha addressed the eight bodhisattva-mahāsattvas:
"If any man or woman practices this divine mantra— writing it down, upholding it,
reading it, reciting it, and explaining it to others— "
In this present life, one obtains five hundred merits.
For example, like a bhikṣu with a mind of loving-kindness,
he will ultimately not be harmed by poison nor struck by weapons.
Fire cannot burn it, water cannot float it away,
and neither kings nor emperors can take advantage of it.
Such is the case for both men and women.
Practicing this *dhāraṇī-sūtra* of the vow-pledge possesses such merit that one shall not be harmed by water or fire,
nor by dragons, lions, tigers, or wolves.
Whether they be *pūtana* spirits or *kumbhāṇḍa* ghosts who delight in harassing people—
whether they wish to kill someone, seize their wealth and treasures,
or destroy their meditative concentration— if one applies this [mantra], even those who intend to cause harm will find no opportunity.
The Buddha said, "What I have spoken is no different from the truth.
It is only that those with past-life karma do not request it.
If a person purely observes the fast and precepts and practices this mantra-sūtra,"
One need not fear eye ailments; with the body free from disease and the mind free from sorrow, one shall ultimately encounter no calamities.
Even when facing matters leading to death, one attains liberation and is no longer subject to affliction or harm.
If any man or woman practices this divine mantra,
they shall be protected and revered by the devas, who will further praise and extol them.
This includes the benevolent dragon kings, ghosts, spirits, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, ghost kings, humans, and non-humans.
Each shall together revere and love them, extolling their virtues;
they shall be protected and mindful of by all Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, Śrāvakas, and the assembly of noble ones.
At the time of their death, these eight great Bodhisattvas will welcome their spirits.
Rebirth in the Western Land will be attained with sovereign ease according to one's wish.
Thereupon, the World-Honored One praised in verse:
"I have expounded the meaning of the mantras for consecration, Which expel all that is evil, malevolent spirits, and ghosts."

Other ghosts and spirits shall find no opportunity; the deity of the knotted thread shall constantly provide protection against the transformations of birds and beasts and the solitary cries of wild creatures.
For those who wear, carry, or recite this, calamities and misfortunes shall be extinguished.
If one travels by boat upon rivers, seas, or oceans, [it shall protect against] the crocodiles, dragons, fish, soft-shelled turtles, and tortoises within the waters.
Though there be various and countless kinds of beings, they shall ultimately do no harm, but cross over in safety.
Even if one enters the homes of heretics or those with malevolent poisons, the medicine within their food and drink will be digested of its own accord;
by wearing this [dhāraṇī], evil may be removed, and those who give rise to jealousy shall have their resentment extinguished.
Enemies will be subdued and face one another with joy; creditors will relax their intent and no longer dispute over wealth.
Profits from buying and selling will naturally increase ten-thousandfold; thieves will not lead one astray, and fear shall be dispelled.
One need have no anxiety regarding death at the hands of officials. If one wears this upon oneself, makes a vow, and spits [upon it], all afflictions shall be removed.
If there are those who give birth, they shall always give birth to sons; should daughters be born, they shall all be upright and dignified.
At the birth canal, demons shall transform into protectors; through even the slightest perils and calamities, none shall fail to be delivered.
Though malevolent spirits may harass, benevolent deities shall assist; freed from all dangers and hardships, one shall be without fear.
The corrupt dragons in the ocean breathe forth foul vapors; though they wish to assault and oppress, they cannot cause harm.
Wandering ghosts and spirits seek to devour humans, but upon seeing one who maintains this vow of binding, they all withdraw and vanish.
When demons and malevolent spirits enter a person's belly, by reciting and maintaining this vow of binding, they shall all exit of their own accord.
In mountain streams, valleys, and vast wildernesses teeming with various venomous insects, by wearing this [sutra] one will not be harmed;
When enemies and bandits from other regions plunder people's wealth, upon seeing one who recites it, they will return home along the road;
In the evil and degenerate final age, when toxic swellings arise, by wearing it and making vows, there shall be nothing that is not extinguished.

If there is a man who studies and recites this *Buddha-spoken Sūtra of the Divine Mantra and Vows*, even if one were to attempt to praise its merit, it would be like removing a single grain of sand from the banks of the Ganges.
Swords, blades, spears, and halberds shall not wound his body; thieves, bandits, and enemies shall be unable to harm him.
The king and his ministers were filled with joy; such is the merit of learning this divine mantra.
Though venomous snakes are truly fearsome, upon seeing one who recites it, their poison and malady are instantly dispelled;
they no longer harbor anger or emit foul breath. Such is the merit of upholding this divine mantra.
Neither enemies nor grudges can cause them harm; when devas, nāgas, spirits, and gandharvas behold their majestic radiance, they remain silent and believe.

Those who study and recite this scripture possess such virtue that even the wild wolves and great pythons of the mountains and forests, as well as lions, fierce tigers, deer, and frogs [are brought under their influence].
Those with no intent to harm yet harbor poison within, and all manner of evils—may Māra dare not oppose them.

When malevolent spirits and ghosts seize the souls of men, the gods and common people who harbor harmful intentions will naturally submit upon sensing his majestic spiritual power. One who studies this and makes this vow shall have nothing to fear.
Such a person shall be free from illness and suffering; their ears and eyes will be keen and clear, without obstruction.
Their speech will be eloquent and wise, distinguished and preeminent. By practicing this divine scripture, they can eliminate evil;
such a person shall never fall into hell, nor enter the realms of hungry ghosts or animals.
In every lifetime one will be born with the knowledge of past lives;
by studying and reciting this sutra, one will be honored by humans and protected by ghosts, spirits, and gandharvas.
The various devas, the four heavenly kings, as well as the asuras and mahoragas—those who practice this divine mantra shall be protected by its merit.
All the devas together extol his virtues; devas, humans, nāgas, yakṣas, and gandharvas praise him, causing his wishes to be fulfilled.
For the sake of others, he recites and expounds the sutras, so that those people’s resolve for the Way shall not regress, and the meaning of Dharma-wisdom shall be inexhaustible.
One whose physical appearance is beautiful and peerless, who recites and studies this sutra to transform and enlighten people—
when nations wage war against one another and the populace falls into chaos, when famine repeatedly strikes and suffering and destitution prevail—
one shall never meet an untimely death therein; such is the power of one who can recite this sutra and transform others.
Valiantly subduing all demonic activities, his mind is fearless and his hair does not stand on end;
his meritorious conduct is inconceivable, as he subdues non-Buddhists and causes them to enter the Right Path.
He overcomes malevolent sorcery, illusions, and incantations, as well as the defiled, heterodox, and improper practices of evil ways.
Holding this divine mantra, none can prevail against it; because it is established through the practice of loving joy in the Dharma, all together sing its virtues.
The disciples of the Buddha, endowed with the wisdom of emptiness, shall appear in the future during the final age, having received in their own hands this Sūtra of the Divine Mantra of Bound Vows.
Always practicing with diligence and joyful exultation, with a single mind and harmonious joy, they shall revere this Dharma;
receiving and upholding this sutra scroll, they shall lecture upon, recite, and chant it.

They shall ensure that these words of the Dharma are not lost, proclaiming them wherever they go so that all may know them widely. As these words of the Dharma circulate, they will bring great benefit.
At that time, having spoken these verses, the World-Honored One addressed Ānanda, saying:
"Suppose there were someone who, having beheld the Buddha face-to-face, made offerings with a sincere heart of robes, food, and drink."
The provision of bedding, the medical treatment for illness and emaciation,
and so forth, are not equal to someone who upholds this *Sūtra of the Consecrated Phrases and the Spirit-Mantra of Vows*,
copying, maintaining, reading, and reciting it.
To record this on bamboo or silk and explain it to others is to provide complete and perfect offerings to the Buddha.
At that time, Śakra, Lord of Devas, arrived together with countless devas.
Each carrying celestial flowers and incense as offerings, they scattered them over the Buddha and addressed him,
saying: "We shall protect and uphold those who maintain and recite this Sūtra of Vows."
The Four Heavenly Kings and the various gods above each brought flowers and incense to make offerings to the Buddha,
and each addressed the Buddha, saying:
I shall protect those good men and good women who receive this sutra,
copy it, uphold it, read and recite it, and explain it to others,
wherever they may travel and dwell.
"Protect them so that no one shall seek to find an opportunity to harm them.

The Buddha told Ānanda: "I now, for you and the fourfold assembly of disciples, shall speak this Great Divine Incantation Sūtra of the Body-Protecting Vow, consisting of the Hundred King Spirits and the Mantras of Consecration."
"You should receive, uphold, and transmit this to men and women alike, causing them to recite it, proclaim my words,
and reveal them to those who have not yet heard them.
Thus did the Buddha speak to the fourfold assembly of devas, nāgas, yakṣas, and śrāvakas.
Upon hearing this sutra, they rejoiced, prostrated themselves, and practiced it accordingly.
*The Fourth Scroll of the Consecration Sutra:

The Sutra Spoken by the Buddha on the Deities Who Guard and Station Themselves Left and Right of the Palace and Dwelling through the Consecration Mantras*. *The Sutra Spoken by the Buddha on the Deities Who Guard and Station Themselves Left and Right of the Palace and Dwelling through the Consecration Mantras*.
Sūtra Scroll Five.
Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Śrīmitra of Central India during the Eastern Jin Dynasty.
Thus have I heard:
At one time the Buddha was staying in the kingdom of Magadha,
together with twelve hundred and fifty bhikṣus and seventeen thousand bodhisattvas.
There were thirty thousand upāsakas, twelve thousand upāsikās,
and an incalculable number of devas, humans, ghosts, spirits, and nāga kings.
They all gathered together to listen to the Buddha’s preaching of the Dharma, and there was none who did not delight in hearing it.
The Buddha said to Maudgalyāyana:
"In the kingdom of Rājagṛha, a thousand li from the city, there are more than seven hundred households."
Having not yet beheld the transformation of the Sages, they do not recognize the True Way.
They frequently serve gods and ghosts, mountain deities, river spirits, tree spirits,
as well as the sun, moon, five planets, the twenty-eight lunar mansions, and the spirits of water and fire.
The entire village served him as their true leader,
making the sacrifice of living beings their constant practice.
At that time, the village chief was a king named Karana.
The household consisted of more than one hundred people, both men and women.
During the spring equinox, they were all tormented by malevolent spirits and ghosts.
This Karana lived on the edge of a mountain valley.
Some say that a mountain deity is harassing me;
some say a tree deity is harassing me;
others say a deity of water, fire, the sun, the moon, or the lunar mansions is harassing me.
Having formed this thought, he was overcome with great sorrow and suffering.
At that time, on the following morning, the evil Māra again brought forth five classes of malevolent spirits,
who all joined their strength together to claw at the earth and cry out loudly.
The entire household of the terrifying Kāraṇa—both great and small—was struck with fear.
Some spirits had bodies like lions;
others were shaped like bears, brown bears, tigers, wolves, elephants, dragons, oxen, horses, dogs, or monkeys—their forms cannot be described in full detail.
Some have the heads of insects and the bodies of humans, with the forms of vipers and snakes and the hands of soft-shelled turtles and tortoises;
some have six eyes and three heads;
others have a single head with three faces, complete with fangs, teeth, claws, and talons.
Some carried mountains and spat fire, with thunder and lightning crashing down;
when the villagers heard of this, there was none who did not share in their distress.
Yet, Karana’s mind was agitated and troubled, and he spoke thus to his kinsmen:
"You all should assist me in devising a plan.
At that time, there was among the villagers a student of the Brahmin path who said to Kālāma, "You may invite the great scholar, the pure-faithed Brahmin."
Kālāna replied, "So be it.
He then selected an auspicious day and favorable hour, prepared a great offering,
and the brahmins assembled at Kālāna’s grand guest hall.
Kālāna himself served the water for washing.
When the serving of water was finished and the meal was concluded,
he spread out a small, low seat and rose from his own.
He addressed the virtuous ones and the brahmins of pure faith:
"Since the spring equinox,
we have been constantly harassed and afflicted by various māras."
"May all the brahmins each manifest their sacred arts to repel the calamities and evil transformations wrought by spirits and ghosts.
Each of the great brahmins spoke thus.
"Excellent, excellent! I shall explain to you the Dharma of our former teacher.
In the past, such a transformation also occurred in the kingdom of Vārāṇasī.
You should [prepare] a level and clean spot within the village."
He offered thanks to the deities of the four mountains, as well as the deities of the sun,
moon, and constellations, saying: "I shall obtain a hundred heads from various sentient beings of diverse species,
along with two young children, to slaughter as an offering to the gods."
"Take all your family members, both great and small,
and go to a level and clean spot within the village to a sacrificial altar;
have every person prostrate themselves there."
"Please command us to seek protection, and only then shall we be at peace.
At that time, Karṇa acted according to these words;
the following morning, he prepared two young children and various other kinds of sentient beings, each numbering one hundred heads.
Having settled the village, he then took his family members, both great and small,
as well as all the sentient beings, and proceeded to that sacrificial altar.
Elephants, horses, oxen, and sheep followed along the road, their mournful cries shaking the great earth.
He was to exit through the eastern gate and proceed to the sacrificial altar.
Thereupon, the World-Honored One, out of great compassion to universally save all sentient beings,
took pity on this Karana for being so exceedingly stubborn and foolish.
"How can one give rise to such great malice as to take the lives of many beings for the sake of wishing to save a single family?
He then commanded his disciple Mahāmaudgalyāyana:
"You should go and act on behalf of Kālāmas."
He spoke the incantation for exorcising ghosts and spirits to protect Kālaṇa.
Maudgalyāyana, having received these instructions,
immediately relied upon the Buddha’s majestic spiritual power to summon the virtuous deities of the five directions for Kālaṇa.
By means of this, the gates and doorways of Karana shall be protected on all sides, and all shall obtain peace and security.
May malevolent spirits and ghosts who come and go be expelled;
as for those who would cause you harm, from this day forward—
"I have kept you far from your village so that no harm might come to you.

When Kālāma saw Maudgalyāyana manifesting his supernatural power by flying through the air, he was filled with joy and leaped for gladness; he prostrated himself, placing his head at Maudgalyāyana’s feet.
He thought to himself: "The Venerable One does not regard me as foolish or lowly;
he has manifested his spiritual power to look upon me and deliver me from calamity, enabling me to find relief and be free once more from sorrow and affliction."
"I have now indeed received the majestic power of the Venerable One;
he has rescued me from peril and caused all the evil māras to hide themselves and remain unseen.
Having spoken these words, Karṇa [ceased].
When all the brahmins saw Maudgalyāyana manifesting his supernatural transformations and coming to recite a great divine mantra for Kālana,
on the day of the incantation, heaven and earth shook violently.
The various brahmins sent Kālana to perform sacrifices to the spirits; however,
the offerings of food and drink, along with their seats,
all flew up and hovered in the void.
All the various beings each attained liberation;
no one remained to obstruct them as they departed following him.
When the brahmins saw Maudgalyāyana manifesting his magical arts, [they were amazed].
Such was the power and majesty of his transformations.

The fourfold assembly, all being thus moved, bowed their heads at the feet of Maudgalyāyana and inquired after his well-being, saying: "Venerable Maudgalyāyana, whom do you honor as your teacher? Whose dharma is so truly sublime as this?"
"You have crushed and extinguished the calamities and transformations brought by us spirits and deities,
causing all the villagers to find relief;
this has come about entirely through the grace of the Venerable One."
Maudgalyāyana said to the brahmin Karṇa and the fourfold assembly:
"My teacher now is the Honored One of gods and humans;
his wisdom is vast and expansive, reaching all things without exception."
He profoundly knows the events of the past and the future.
His body is sixteen feet tall and the color of purple-polished gold,
adorned with the thirty-two marks of a great man.
He delivers people from calamities and hardships, such that none fail to attain liberation.
When the fourfold assembly heard of the Great Sage’s majestic spiritual power,
there was no one among them who did not wish to behold the body of the World-Honored One.
Kālāna said to Maudgalyāyana, "Can the Buddha,
the World-Honored One, be seen now?
Maudgalyāyana replied, "The Buddha, the World-Honored One, is currently staying near Rājagṛha."
He preached the true and wondrous Dharma for the devas, humans,
and the fourfold assembly of disciples. Kālāma said to Mahāmaudgalyāyana,
"I now wish to follow you and go to see the World-Honored One."
Maudgalyāyana said, "The Buddha’s supernormal powers and holy penetration are such that he perceives your mind directly; there is no need for you to go.
You need only burn incense and scatter flowers."
The World-Honored One’s manifestation of supernatural transformations today is likewise.
Before long, Kāraṇa, merely burn incense, scatter flowers, and mindfully recollect the Buddha with a tranquil heart.
In a brief moment, the Buddha will manifest his supernatural power and arrive.
Accompanied by twelve hundred and fifty bhikṣus and the fourfold assembly of disciples,
as well as an incalculable number of bodhisattvas,
they all gathered together in the great guest hall of Karanda.
The guest hall spontaneously became vast, spacious, and magnificent, transforming into a palace.
Its pillars and beams were all made of lapis lazuli,
adorned with the seven treasures, and hung with various banners and canopies.
On all four sides were various minor bodhisattvas,
holding banners and canopies and standing in attendance to the left and right.
Kāraṇa, the brahmins, and the fourfold assembly beheld the Buddha.
With immeasurable joy and exultation in his heart,
he bowed his head to touch the Buddha’s feet and prostrated himself in salutation.
Karana then stepped forward, knelt with his right knee on the ground, and joined his palms in reverence.
He addressed the Buddha, saying, "World-Honored One,
since the beginning of kalpas,
I have believed in heterodox and inverted views, failing to recognize what is true and correct."
On days of peril and distress, people would habitually slaughter sentient beings to seek blessings and protection.
Now, the World-Honored One, with great compassion and universal salvation,
rescues and delivers sentient beings from the afflictions of danger and distress.
All have received liberation and are freed from all terrors;
this is entirely due to the grace of Maudgalyāyana, the God among Gods.
Both the members of the household, great and small, and the people of the village have all attained deliverance.
Kālāma and the fourfold assembly of brahmins requested from the Buddha the method for receiving the precepts.
The Buddha extensively explained for them the causes and conditions of karmic actions, whereby they attained the purity of the Dharma-eye.
The members of the royal clan, both great and small, as well as the villagers,
heard the sound of the Dharma and rejoiced, each giving rise to a virtuous mind;
some received the precepts, while others were reborn in the heavens.
Each attains the Way differently according to their respective karmic actions. At that time, there was a bodhisattva among those seated named Puguān (Universal Observation).
He rose from his seat, stepped forward, and addressed the Buddha, saying:
The World-Honored One has already expounded for Kāraṇa the incantations for warding off malevolent spirits in the five directions,
completing the protection of the gates and the stationing of guards on both sides.
I only pray that you would further expound upon the verses and phrases previously spoken by Maudgalyāyana for the sake of all sentient beings in future ages.
If there should be those who are afflicted by malevolent spirits such as the Kārāṇas,
I shall write down, uphold, read, and recite this sutra text to show it to future generations,
widely proclaiming and circulating it so that it may be heard far and near.
All shall attain liberation and no longer have any anxiety or fear.
The Buddha told the Bodhisattva Puguān:
"You are able, for the sake of the future age of turbidity and evil..."
Regarding the question again concerning the divine names of the unsurpassed chapter on consecration:
listen attentively and bear this in mind, for I shall further expound such verses.
The Bodhisattva Puguang replied, "Yes, yes, Celestial Honored One."
The fourfold assembly thirsts for this teaching and yearns for it; we pray only that you will speak of it swiftly.
The Buddha said: "The name of the consecrated chapter is as follows:
the spirit is named Aśvaka, the bhikṣuṇī is named Bandhumatī, and the spirit is named Pāṭaliputra. Next...
The spirit named Uṣaṇācī; the Gandharva spirit named Khanilīya;
the Pannila spirit named Ahuramizda; the spirit named Kairīmaiti-parāmiti;
the spirit named Dhara-dhruva-puṇa-khani; and the spirit named Śarādhara-manda.
The name of the Rākṣasa deity is Kūṭidantī; the name of the Yakṣa deity is Vajriṇī; the name of the Kimnara deity is Āpātī;
the name of the Mahoraga deity is Lambapāda; the name of the Gandharva deity is Mukhamaṇḍika; the name of the Asura deity is Jambha; the name of the Preta deity is Bhīma;

"All burial mounds and stupas are inhabited by hosts of both benevolent and malevolent spirits and deities.
The Śākya youth spoke again to the Buddha, saying,
"For what reason are there these benevolent and malevolent spirits and deities within the burial mounds and stupas?"
The Buddha said, "Young man, as for my stūpa,
there are relics of my true body within this stūpa. The Four Heavenly Kings,
the various deities, and the gods of the Heaven of the Thirty-three [are present there]."
Regardless of whether it was day or night, they scattered fine powdered incense and various kinds of famous flowers over the stupas and reliquaries,
and performed celestial music as an offering.
Furthermore, there were the benevolent deities Maheśvara, Maṇibhadra, Śūdra, Śūlika, and Gandharva;
the eight classes of spirits and ghosts, the five rākṣasa spirits,
and the spirit Kumbhāṇḍī with her five hundred sons.
Day and night, without ceasing, may you constantly manifest your majestic spiritual power to protect and mind my stūpas,
so that no malevolent or heterodox spirits and deities may cause harm.
Furthermore, may those evil sentient beings and non-Buddhist heretics with false views who wish to destroy it not be able to invade or ruin my stūpas and temples.
Should any with malicious intent come toward this stūpa, [may they be prevented].
These spirits and deities, by means of their supernatural powers, shall suppress all malevolent intentions and cause the heads of those evil sentient beings to split into seven pieces.
The Buddha further told the youth: "When my stupas and temples exist for five hundred years..."
For nine hundred years, many people made offerings and none would violate or destroy them; yet at that time, the bhikṣus did not cultivate the fast-day precepts (upoṣadha-śīla).
Even among those who did observe them, they were merely jealous of one another.
People greedy for gain and offerings are unwilling to seek my true Way with a sincere heart;
consequently, the stupas and temples will gradually fall into ruin,
and the majestic power of the guardian deities protecting them will diminish.
When one thousand years have passed, there will be bhikṣus who take pleasure in practicing the arts of war;
they will align themselves with kings, princes, ministers,
and subjects to destroy my Dharma.
Consequently, hereafter they shall encounter evil friends who will sever and extinguish my Dharma;
stupas and images will fall into ruin and lose their divine efficacy.
You should know that the benevolent deities will no longer provide protection.
Therefore, they will cause it to be destroyed without anyone to restrain them.
For this reason, you should know that my Dharma-transformation will gradually perish here.
The Buddha told the Śākya youths: "After my parinirvāṇa..."
There are seven reasons why stūpas and monuments fall into ruin:
first, the benevolent deities no longer provide protection;
second, my Dharma naturally intends to perish in its time.
Third, groups of evil bhikṣus will act contrary to the Dharma with one another.
Fourth, they will fail to practice the precepts and violate that which they have received.
Fifth, they will slander one another, thereby destroying my Dharma scriptures.
Sixth, the disciples of the fourfold assembly study various heterodox paths;
they employ talismans, scripts, and prohibitive incantations for the purpose of subduing [demons], yet do not return to the True Dharma.
Seventh, my Dharma is about to perish.
When you encounter an evil king who destroys my Dharma—
demolishing stupas, exterminating the Sangha, and causing the sacred pillars to disappear—
you should know that such calamities will occur when my Dharma has passed a thousand years.
The youth of the Śākya clan spoke again to the Buddha, saying:
"For what reason do these various classes of ghosts and spirits come to rely upon the stupas of ordinary worldlings?
The Buddha replied to the youth: "I have already explained this previously."
Regarding the spirits that inhabit the tombs and stupas of ordinary people,
they are all either the essences of the five grains, malevolent ghosts (*bhūta*), enchanters (*māyāvin*), or transformations;
or else they are the ghosts of those who died untimely deaths.
They have no point of attachment and rely on this as their spirit;
they may be the essences of trees, forests, or mountains.
Having neither food nor drink, they frequent the human world.
They manifest various strange transformations to terrify and agitate people;
when ordinary beings hear of or see them,
they immediately seek blessings from them, calling them "gods."
The youth of the Śākya clan again addressed the Buddha, saying:
"By what means should one restrain them?
How may evil and wickedness be severed so that malevolent spirits are extinguished?"
Poisonous vapors will not circulate, and you shall obtain auspicious merit.
The Buddha said to the Śākya youth:
"You should listen attentively and contemplate this with single-minded focus."
I possess this unsurpassed chapter of consecration mantras,
which eliminates malevolent spirits and ensures that no demons dare to oppose it.
You should recite, uphold, and never forget it.
The youth asked the Buddha, "What is this?
The Buddha told the youth, "Listen attentively and receive it with care;
such is the name of this consecrated chapter."

Having spoken these words, [Ānanda] asked, "What shall this be named, and how should it be practiced?

The Buddha preached the Dharma for the eight classes of beings, including devas and nāgas;
humans, spirits, and ghosts each attained the Way according to their respective karmic conditions, though their realizations differed.

Thereupon, the Brahma King rose from his seat,
knelt with palms joined, and addressed the Buddha,

There are those who, due to subtle causes and conditions, take refuge in many [deities].
Furthermore, seeing that all people undergo suffering and affliction,
their minds are filled with doubt and they cannot reach a definitive understanding.
Now, desiring to rely upon the power of the Buddha’s majestic spiritual authority,

I only pray that the World-Honored One will grant permission for this matter.
He further spoke these words:
"I have often seen the various followers of heterodox paths, numbering ninety-five kinds,
each possessing diverse arts with which they resolve the doubts of others."
"Now, for the World-Honored One, the Perfectly Awakened One, there is no dharma higher than this.

The Buddha said, "Brahmā King, excellent, excellent!"
You are able, for the sake of sentient beings in the future five-turbidity evil age during the period of Semblance Dharma— who harbor many doubts and suspicions,

Since you, out of compassion, wish to speak for our sake, it is excellent, Brahmā; I join you in your joy.
It is well, Brahmā; speak as you please.
Upon hearing the Buddha’s praise of the *Cai jing*, the Brahma King was filled with joy and leaped for gladness.

He expounded one hundred verses from the *Bok-kyeong* (The Scripture of Divination) to demonstrate it to the myriad people,

Now, he explains the hexagrams by means of these verses, saying:
If one hears this Buddha’s incantation sūtra, All hundred demons will vanish their forms;
One’s dwelling shall attain peace and security, And no calamities from officials shall arise.
Dedicated toward the unsurpassed Way, The Brahmā and Indra heavens shall flourish with glory.
In official service one attains high promotion, and from generation to generation gains a virtuous reputation;
yet, though one may possess a good heart, if one cannot rectify the foundation,
and if one’s offerings lack single-minded devotion, one’s merit will diminish day by day.
If one’s previous conduct was unwholesome, it is not too late to reform;
now let all things be auspicious, and fortune and rank will naturally return.
Because one lacked merit and blessings in a former life, one has consequently fallen into these states of suffering.
Lacking faith in the Triple Gem, one who treats the Hero of the World with derision and arrogance will encounter suffering in this very life; thereafter, when life comes to its end,
their accumulated sins will be like a mountain, and the retribution of karma is truly inexhaustible.
If you wish to seek blessings and protection, Repent and offer incense;
Śakra will always assist you. Wherever you go, all shall be auspicious;
Pestilence and poison will naturally vanish, And until the end, no calamity shall remain.
May you enjoy such blessings in every lifetime, And attain rebirth in the heavenly realms.
Fearing that this may not be accomplished, In the end, you will be mourned by others;
Death shall not be yours alone, As weeping and wailing shall fill the months and years.
This is the work of Māra and the heterodox; thus you have suddenly vanished from here.
If you can maintain mindfulness of the Triple Gem, you shall again attain freedom from all defilement.
Your nature has always been kind and affectionate; for what reason have you given rise to resentment and malice?
One who laughs lightly at śramaṇas, thinking they are merely like those entrusted with worldly affairs,
shall receive retribution in life after life; in the end, they will be plundered by the wicked,
and when traveling on the road, they will constantly be bound by the officials of the state.
I am mindful of your youth and the suffering of being orphaned; you have stood firm at the gate of the Way, maintaining a correct mind with harmony and compliance.
Do not cause others to harbor resentment or thoughts of retribution;
let your heart be free from deficiency or excess, and blessings and rank shall be added to your descendants.
Peaceful and free from illness—know this to be the grace of Brahmā.
Having already fallen into the midst of transgressions, one further misleads others through sin;
as calamities and misfortunes become intertwined, all are the result of causes from past lives.
One may together cultivate right practice, Dedicate one’s mind to training with diligence;

By preserving this, one attains liberation. Those who distance themselves from the body of hell And do not wish to practice benevolence and righteousness, Taking deception as their constant priority— [such people cannot attain it].
If one enters the rivers, seas, or oceans, And encounters a wind that prevents them from moving forward,
They will drift aimlessly with the current; When waves and winds overturn their ship,
they are submerged in the water— How could their lives possibly be preserved?
Possessing a heart of noble goodness and a desire for a good reputation and prosperity,
one cultivates all correct practices; thus, life after life, one receives its blessings,
remaining peaceful, secure, and effortless, while friends and kin are likewise joyful and harmonious.
No aspiration made shall fail to bear fruit; what you seek shall swiftly be realized as desired.
If you wish to travel far for trade and seek various treasures, do not act with a lack of compassion, lest you encounter misfortune along the way.
Focusing the mind on the Buddha, one swiftly attains the unsurpassed path;
in every lifetime, one reaps the fruit of reward, living in peace and reaching old age.
But the arrogant one acts as a teacher to Māra, instructing others to kill living beings.
Since karmic retribution is inexhaustible, once one enters the dark realm of the netherworld, malevolent spirits cannot offer protection;
calamities and misfortunes arise in a hundred ways.
One should take refuge in the Triple Gem, for it alone can deliver one from the suffering of sin. This is called [the name of the teaching].
If one's only son commits the five heinous crimes, he will bring calamity and disaster upon you;
he will plunder people's wealth and property, and his bones and remains will be scattered and lost in the desolate wilderness, left exposed so that they cannot be buried.
Life after life one has not seen what is good, wandering instead within the hells.
Now that you have been able to develop a virtuous mind, you should fully exert your efforts;
why dwell in such desolation? It is but a weary labor to guard emptiness.

This will cause you to obtain wealth and treasures, and thereafter bring auspiciousness.

Those who suffer are not merely individuals; rather, their loss of nature arises from causes in previous lives, which is why their lives are brought to peril.

Binding your three souls and seven spirits within this empty mountain.

Brahmā has spoken this divine strategy, so that demonic evils may not arise.

Breaking the fast and violating the sutras and precepts,

Brahmā and Śakra speak this truth to you: be careful not to harbor doubts.

may the teachings spread throughout the lineage of the patriarchs. Even if the gods Brahmā and Śakra are noisy and clamorous, and even if supernatural powers vary in their magnitude, do not give rise to a lack of faith.

What is sought is beset by many obstacles; illnesses cannot be cured.

Observing the fasts and precepts to perform a dharma assembly, one seeks self-realization with the heart.

The sovereign protects and mindfully attends to them, regarding them as if they were pearls and jade;

so that their aspirations shall never suffer humiliation or ruin.
One should simply cultivate virtuous conduct; upon death, one will not enter hell.

being perverse and prone to reviling, causing alarm to the four neighbors;

Ānanda asked, "What is its name? Please tell it to me."
The Bodhisattva Jue said, "The names of these consecrated verses are as follows:

the spirit named Kumbhīra; the spirit named Hāṭaka; the spirit named Mekhala; the spirit named Andhara; the spirit named Maṇira; the spirit named Śuṅgira; the spirit named Indira; the spirit named Pāyara; the spirit named Mahura; the spirit named Candra; the spirit named Jotira; the spirit named Vighna. The Bodhisattva Jue then spoke to Ānanda:
These spirits and deities had seven thousand others as their retinue;
they all joined their palms, bowed their heads,
and listened as the Buddha, the World-Honored One, preached this [Sūtra] on the Medicine Master Lapis Lazuli Light.
By the merit of the Tathāgata’s original vows,
there is not one who does not simultaneously cast off their ghostly or divine form to receive a human body,
attaining long-term liberation and freedom from all afflictions and calamities.
If, on a day of sudden illness or urgent distress,
one should tie the person's name into a cord of five colors;
once their wish has been fulfilled, one should then untie the knot so that the person may obtain [the benefit].
The ritual procedure for the dhāraṇī-mantra of the Empowerment of Merit should be performed in this manner.
Then he spoke the mantra:
*Namo piśāca-kulaveḷūliya pāpahara-saya tadyathā | piśāca piśāca svabhāgate svāhā.* When the Buddha had spoken this sūtra,
The community of bhikṣus numbered eight thousand;
the bodhisattvas numbered thirty-six thousand.
Among the devas, nāgas, yakṣas, and the other eight classes of beings, there were none who did not rejoice.
Ānanda rose from his seat, approached the Buddha, and said to him:
"What should this Dharma teaching be named?
The Buddha said: "This sutra has three names in total."
First is titled "The Merit of the Original Vows of the Medicine Master Lapis Lazuli Light Buddha";
second is titled "The Consecration Verses and the Spirit-King Incantation of the Twelve Oaths";
third is titled "Extradicating Past Transgressions and Attaining Deliverance from Birth and Death."
When the Buddha had finished preaching this sutra, the great assembly of people paid their respects and practiced it accordingly.
*The Consecration Sutra*, Volume Twelve.
